title: Band-9 Samples: Do you have a favorite song you like listening to? [Why/why not?]
content:
This post contains ideas and band-9 sample answers (audio included) for the Cambridge IELTS 12 Academic Speaking Part 1 Question 3 Test 2 question:

“Do you have a favorite song you like listening to? [Why/why not?]”

Sample 1: Yes

“Roar” by Katy Perry holds a special place in my playlist. This song is more than just a catchy tune to me – it’s an empowering anthem that inspires resilience and courage. Perry’s strong vocals, coupled with the song’s energetic beat, make it an invigorating listen. Whenever I face challenges in life, this song serves as a reminder of my own strength and ability to overcome obstacles. It’s like a musical pep-talk, always there to boost my confidence and determination.

Sample 2: Yes

Indeed, I do have a song that I listen to often, and that’s “Perfect” by Ed Sheeran. It’s not just a song, but more like a beacon guiding me towards love. The heartfelt lyrics and touching melody inspire me to seek out love in my own life and to be open to the possibility of finding that special someone. Every time I hear it, I’m reminded that love could be just around the corner, waiting to be discovered.

Sample 3: Yes

You know, I find it really challenging to single out one song as my favorite. But if there’s one artist whose music resonates with me, it’s Taylor Swift. Her voice carries a distinctive charm, and each song of hers resonates with a different aspect of my life. Though the exact titles may not always be at the tip of my tongue, the emotional connection I share with her music is potent and enduring.

Sample 4: No

I don’t believe I have a single favorite song, but rather a compilation of many that I hold dear. Each song in my playlist offers a unique flavor, and together, they create a musical journey I thoroughly enjoy. The variety keeps me engaged and prevents any single song from becoming monotonous.

Sample 5: No

No, I don’t have a particular song that I would single out as my favorite. The reason being, my musical taste is quite impermanent, often changing with new discoveries. Today’s favorite song might be forgotten tomorrow when I stumble upon a different, equally captivating tune.

Sample 6: No

Interestingly, I don’t have a favorite song as my engagement with music is largely passive. I typically use it as background noise that fills the silence while I focus on other tasks. It’s more about creating an ambiance than actually listening to the lyrics or melody, hence I rarely pay enough attention to distinguish one song from another.

Sample 7: Not Remembering

At this present time, it’s quite challenging for me to pinpoint a specific song that I hold dear. You see, my life is filled to the brim with a wide array of responsibilities and duties. These commitments have somewhat muddled my memory, making it hard to identify one track that I would call my favorite.

Sample 8: Not Remembering

At present, I’m at a loss to identify a particular song that I consider my favorite. It’s quite peculiar, but my memory seems to play tricks on me when it comes to music. I can become engrossed in a tune, listening to it repetitively for days, only to have the details fade away. The rhythm, the lyrics, and often, even the artist, just seem to evaporate from my memory.

Sample 9: It Depends

I wouldn’t say I have a favorite song because my music preference fluctuates with my mood. Sometimes I find comfort in the soothing notes of classical music, other times I’m energized by the vibrant beats of pop. So, it’s more about what resonates with my feelings at a particular moment rather than sticking to one favorite track.

Sample 10: It Depends

Actually, I don’t think I can nominate a particular song as my all-time favorite. My preferred music track tends to change as I progress through different life phases. For instance, in my youth, I was captivated by the catchy and high-energy pop tunes as they ignited the enthusiasm of young age. However, now, I find myself gravitating towards mellower, more meaningful songs that resonate with my current experiences. So, my so-called ‘favorite’ is really a mirror reflecting my life’s journey.
